title: MLR Requirements and Profit Limits
summary: Explains Medicaid MCO Medical Loss Ratio requirements, how MLR is calculated, reporting obligations, and the implications of failing to meet the 85% floor.
objectives: Calculate MLR using the standard Medicaid formula
Explain what expenses qualify as clinical versus administrative under MLR rules
Describe the consequences when an MCO's MLR falls below 85%

content_blocks.body:
The 2016 Medicaid managed care final rule set an 85% medical loss ratio (MLR) standard for MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs: states must set capitation rates so each plan can reasonably achieve an MLR of at least 85%, and any minimum MLR a state imposes must be at least 85%.

MLR = (Incurred Claims + Quality Improvement Expenditures + Fraud Prevention Activities) / (Premium Revenue − Taxes and Licensing/Regulatory Fees)

If a state requires remittance, a plan whose MLR falls below the state's minimum must pay back the difference. States can also set minimums above 85% in their contracts.
content_blocks.heading: The 85% MLR Floor

content_blocks.body: If a state requires remittance and an MCO's annual MLR falls below the 85% threshold, the plan must remit the shortfall to the state Medicaid agency. For example, if a plan received $500 million in capitation and achieved an 82% MLR, it would owe the state $15 million (3% × $500M). States must report MLR data to CMS annually. Unlike ACA marketplace MLR rebates, Medicaid MLR remittances go to the state, not directly to beneficiaries.
